requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County Office of the Tax Collector (Tax Collector Dariel Fernandez)
requirements.applies_when: Any business operating at a place of business in Miami-Dade County; a separate receipt is required for each place of business and for each separate local business tax classification at the same location. Restaurants are a regulated food-service classification.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. Ch. 205 (state authorization); Miami-Dade County Code Ch. 8A, including s. 8A-175 (renewal/penalties)

forms.name: New Business Tax Receipt application (online via BTExpress; paper application also accepted by mail or in person at 200 NW 2nd Ave., Miami, FL 33128)

requirements.notes: Valid for one tax year: October 1 – September 30. Renewal deadline September 30; delinquency penalties: 10% added in October, plus 5% per additional month (capped at 25%); per Fla. Stat. 205.053(3) an additional penalty of up to $250 may apply if the tax is unpaid 150 days after the initial notice of tax due. Receipts are transferable on change of ownership, location, or trade name. County-issued fee amounts by classification were not published on the pages read.
requirements.timeline: Apply online via BTExpress; allow 3–5 business days for staff review after application submittal and any follow-up steps. Note: pursuant to section 205.0532, Florida Statutes (HB 905, effective July 1, 2026), applicants must complete a Cuba-transaction attestation; the receipt is printable up to three (3) business days after attestation.
requirements.title: Miami-Dade County Local Business Tax Receipt (county-level)

requirements.agency: The municipality where the business is located (e.g., City of Miami); county layer issued by the Miami-Dade County Tax Collector
requirements.applies_when: Any business located inside an incorporated municipality (including the City of Miami) — the county receipt alone is not enough.
requirements.citation: County requirement to hold both: Miami-Dade County Tax Collector service page; City of Miami Code Enforcement FAQ

forms.name: City business tax receipt application (issued by each municipality under its own code, e.g. City of Miami Code Ch. 31)

requirements.notes: The county's own page states: 'Businesses located within a municipality must obtain both a city receipt and a Miami-Dade County receipt.' The City of Miami (Department of Code Enforcement FAQ) confirms the city layer: to operate a business in the City you must apply for a Certificate of Use (CU) and a Business Tax Receipt (BTR). So a restaurant in the City of Miami needs (at minimum): City of Miami CU + City of Miami BTR + Miami-Dade County BTR, plus the state DBPR food-service license layer.
requirements.title: Municipal (city) Business Tax Receipt — stacking with the county receipt

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources (RER), Zoning / Development Services
requirements.applies_when: Before opening any business in unincorporated Miami-Dade County. Triggered by: establishment of a new business at a location, relocation of an existing business, change in business use or operation, expansion of use/operation, temporary uses exceeding 45 days, and any change of business name or ownership.
requirements.citation: Miami-Dade County Code Ch. 33 (Land Development Code); CU requirement stated on RER certificates page

forms.name: Application for Certificate of Use (includes business information, folio number, square footage, nature of business)

requirements.notes: The CU confirms the business is allowed in the zoning district and that the structure holds a proper Certificate of Occupancy for the use, and certifies compliance with local zoning/environmental ordinances, the Florida Fire Prevention Code, and the Florida Building Code. Operating without a CU can draw a fine/ticket to both the business owner and the property owner. Restaurant-specific: applicants must submit a business process letter explaining the business use (for restaurants: whether dinnerware is disposable or metal/ceramic, indoor/outdoor seating area, etc.) plus any applicable DERM Operating Permit applications. A Certificate of Occupancy is a prerequisite to obtaining a CU (for buildouts, the building permit + CO must be issued first). Contacts: RER-CUINFO@miamidade.gov, 786-315-2660; MeetQ consults available. Fees exist (non-refundable upfront fee plus remainder on approval) but amounts were not published on the pages read.
requirements.title: Certificate of Use (CU) — unincorporated Miami-Dade County

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources (RER), Building/Permit Section
requirements.applies_when: New construction, remodeling/renovation, or change of use — e.g., converting a school or retail space into a restaurant. Required before a Certificate of Use can be issued.
requirements.citation: Florida Building Code; Miami-Dade County Code Ch. 8 (Building); RER certificates page

forms.name: Building permit application; online Certificate of Occupancy/Completion lookup and application portal

requirements.notes: A CO validates that the building (or renovation project) was completed in compliance with applicable codes; a CC is for fences, windows, shell buildings. A fee plus approved inspections and completion holds are required. Contact for CO/CC: RER-SPA@miamidade.gov, 786-315-2100.
requirements.title: Certificate of Occupancy / Completion (CO/CC) prerequisite for restaurant buildouts

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources (RER), Division of Environmental Resources Management (DERM)
requirements.applies_when: Businesses opening, relocating, changing use, expanding, or changing ownership inside a Miami-Dade municipality (the 'Municipal Certificate of Use' track). The county reviews before the municipality issues its CU or business license.
requirements.citation: Miami-Dade County Code Ch. 24 (Environmental Protection Ordinance); DERM Environmental Plan Review

forms.name: Miami-Dade County Approval of Municipal Certificate of Use application (signed by municipal official/staff) + executed lease showing square footage/unit/usage + business process letter + any applicable DERM Operating Permit applications

requirements.notes: DERM's Environmental Plan Review reviews building permits, Certificates of Use and Occupancy, and Local Business Tax applications for compliance with federal, state, and county environmental laws (Ch. 24). For restaurants, DERM Operating Permit applications (e.g., the FOG/GDO permit) may be required as part of the CU/BTR package. DERM contact: DERMPlanReview@miamidade.gov, 786-315-2800. So even inside the City of Miami, the county retains an environmental review touchpoint.
requirements.title: Municipal Certificate of Use — county environmental (DERM) review for businesses inside municipalities

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade Fire Rescue Department, Fire Prevention Division
requirements.applies_when: All businesses in Miami-Dade County (including restaurants) must undergo inspection and receive a Life Safety Operating Permit for Florida Fire Prevention Code compliance.
requirements.citation: Miami-Dade County Code Ch. 14 (Fire Prevention); Florida Fire Prevention Code

forms.name: Life Safety inspection request (online); Fire Inspection and Permitting Internet Payment Site

requirements.notes: Businesses needing inspection may request one online or by contacting the Fire Prevention Division (786-331-4800). The specific fee amounts per occupancy/restaurant classification were not published on the pages read; the Fire Prevention Fee Schedule is set by Implementing Order. NOTE: a September 2026 county ordinance amending Ch. 14 reportedly shifted fire inspections for small business occupancies from annual to biennial — this came from a non-official news source and needs confirmation against the current county code (see open questions).
requirements.timeline: Inspection required; the permit is issued upon compliance with any pending violations and payment of the required fee (per MDFR payment site, referencing Implementing Order 4-123). Inspections are conducted in order of priority based on occupancy type.
requirements.title: Life Safety Operating Permit — Miami-Dade Fire Rescue annual inspection

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade Fire Rescue Department, Fire Prevention Division
requirements.applies_when: All commercial buildings — new construction or remodeling of existing construction (e.g., a restaurant buildout or kitchen renovation). Single-family homes are not inspected.
requirements.citation: Miami-Dade County Code Ch. 14; Florida Fire Prevention Code

forms.name: New construction fire inspection request; Fire Rescue Permit Forms & Checklists

requirements.notes: Separate from the annual Life Safety Operating Permit: MDFR performs the Certificate of Occupancy inspections for commercial construction and remodel work. Fees per Implementing Order 4-123 (not published on pages read).
requirements.title: Fire Prevention Division Certificate of Occupancy inspections for restaurant construction/remodels

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources (RER), Division of Environmental Resources Management (DERM)
requirements.applies_when: Any non-residential facility that handles, prepares or processes food (hot or cold) and discharges or has the potential to discharge fats, oil and grease to the public sanitary sewer system. Restaurants are listed as typical FOG generators (along with cafeterias, supermarkets, schools, banquet halls, food courts).
requirements.citation: Miami-Dade County Code Ch. 24 (Environmental Protection Ordinance)

forms.name: FOG Discharge Control / Grease Discharge Operating Permit application (GDO permit lookup/renewal portal)

requirements.notes: Requires both an approved, installed grease trap/interceptor and the operating permit itself. DERM regulates grease traps through its FOG program (a federal court-order consent decree context). This is a distinct restaurant-critical county layer beyond the state DBPR food-service license.
requirements.timeline: The permit must be obtained and maintained; facilities with GDO permit class OP (operator) or GENOP (generator/operator) must file a Liquid Waste Transporter Electronic Manifest on or before the 20th of the month in which the FOG control device is cleaned.
requirements.title: Fats, Oil and Grease (FOG) Discharge Control / Grease Discharge Operating (GDO) Permit — DERM

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources (RER), Development Services Division
requirements.applies_when: Installing signs exempted from building permits by the Florida Building Code but subject to county zoning review under Miami-Dade Code s. 33-8.1: e.g., balloon signs, flat wall signs up to 40 sq ft and 30 ft building height (county-approved detail only), painted wall signs, stick-on fabric letters, window graphics and vinyl wall signs up to 40 sq ft. Larger/structural signs require full building permits instead.
requirements.citation: Miami-Dade County Code s. 33-8.1 (ZIP standards); sign regulations of the underlying zoning district (Ch. 33)
requirements.notes: ZIP assistance: RER-ZIP@miamidade.gov, 786-315-2660; MeetQ consults available. Sign rules inside municipalities (e.g., City of Miami) are set by the municipality's own code — the county ZIP applies in unincorporated areas.
requirements.title: Zoning Improvement Permit (ZIP) for restaurant storefront signage
